findings.summary: The historical Constituents file (built on the 2026-01 ticker list) keeps later joiners that changed ticker after joining in every snapshot back to 2015-01-02: DAY (joined as CDAY 2021-09-20), CPAY (FLT 2018-06-20), EG (RE 2017-06-19), WTW (WLTW 2016-01-05), IQV (Q 2017-08-29), SW (2024-07-08). 5,661 pre-join member-sessions have price bars, so these names were eligible in backtests before they were members.
evidence: Removals followed by re-adds (EQT, PCG, FSLR) are represented correctly: 0 member sessions inside their gaps.
findings.follow_up: Separate issue: correct the historical Constituents rows with S&P-sourced effective dates, then backtest A/B (changes the research universe).

findings.summary: COL.csv is not Rockwell Collins: closes 0.01-0.85 with volumes of a few hundred shares, while COL was a member 2015-01-02..2018-11-30. NFX.csv (Newfield, member until 2019) and AVB.csv (member until 2026-08-17) continue with bars of the securities that reused or absorbed the symbol, appended by the daily update.
findings.follow_up: Quarantine or truncate in a separate data correction; the daily update should refuse to append when the provider identity changes.

findings.summary: Some migrated files end with flat zero-volume bars after trading stopped (TWX 2018-06-15, AET 2018-11-29); the audit counts them as valid bars.
findings.follow_up: Treat zero-volume flat bars after a documented close of trading as absent in a later audit revision.

findings.summary: The daily update only appends rows, so splits after the first download leave artificial jumps (APH 2026-09-03, KLAC 2026-06-12, CRWD 2026-07-02, CVNA 2026-05-08, MNST 2026-08-11, BKNG 2026-04-06, DD reverse 2026-06-24). The gap filter then excludes these names for about 90 sessions.
findings.follow_up: Separate issue (outside #50): re-download full history on provider corporate actions; repair the affected files through staging.
